cause_trace.step: Each new part is wrapped in default 4096-byte bufio.Reader. ReadHeader/decoding see the logical EOF produced by boundaryReader.
Mid-first-fill delimiter/terminator matches return buffered n>0, io.EOF and clear atPartStart=false, but do not consume the marker in the underlying parent reader.
The subsequent Next FIRST drains current part using io.Copy(io.Discard,b), then scans delimiter lines. This was omitted in V1/V2 slice traversal.

During that drain atPartStart=false, non-CR/LF positions no longer match markers. Shifted/mid-line marker and apparent following MIME headers are discarded until a recognized CR/LF boundary candidate. They do not allocate child nodes.

V2 advanced directly to line-Next at the logical EOF cursor, so counted a phantom sibling at the mid-line delimiter (24 offset leaves + Compatibility14/15). Mid-line terminators could instead prematurely stop and undercount later real CRLF children. V3 explicitly performs post-EOF discard with firstFill=false whenever nonempty bytes were delivered, before line-Next.
